templates._comment: Procedural mission templates (src/systems/MissionGenerator.js). Each template's roles are filled from the live world (npcs.json members, relationships and request pools; map.json areas; schedule.json matches; InventorySystem ITEMS) and every result is checked with MissionValidation before it is offered. Gates: minDay, minRank (index into shift.ranks), hours, weather, afterRain, events (EventSystem ids). cooldownDays keeps the same template + key roles from repeating for N days. Text fills: {role}, {role.first}, {role.label}, {Role} (capitalised), {court.time}. Dialogue text may be a string, a list (random pick) or an archetype / npc-id map with '*' as the default. greet / idle / thanks add one of the speaker's own npcs.json lines.

choices.label: Suggest Coach Rafa assesses him
choices.result: An expert opinion suits her perfectly. She books Coach Rafa for a "proper assessment" this evening. Theo looks like he might faint.

choices.label: Stay out of family business
choices.result: You make polite noises about the weather. Mrs. Wellington signs Theo up for another lunch. Theo sees it all from behind the fountain.

missions.title: Theo's Exhibition Set
missions.description: Coach Rafa has arranged an exhibition set for Theo on Court 1 and Mrs. Wellington is coming to watch. Set the court up properly.

steps.prompt: Talk to Coach Rafa about the exhibition.
Collect fresh towels from the pro shop.
Lay the towels out on Court 1.
Check in with Mrs. Wellington after the set.

missions.title: The Brandt Line Call
missions.description: Newlyweds Leo and Harper Brandt need a neutral party for a disputed line call on Court 2. It's 'for the marriage'.

choices.label: It clipped the line. In.
choices.result: Harper cheers. Leo stares at the line for a long time, then laughs. "Okay, counsel. Your point."

choices.label: Out, by a hair.
choices.result: Leo pumps his fist like he won Wimbledon. Harper narrows her eyes and adds a tally mark to her spreadsheet.

choices.label: Too close to call. Play a let.
choices.result: They replay the point. Harper lobs him again, clearly in this time. Leo applauds. Both look delighted.

missions.title: Six-Month Anniversary
missions.description: Harper is planning a surprise picnic by the fountain for her and Leo's six-month anniversary. Leo thinks she forgot.

steps.prompt: Pick up the sparkling water Jess is hiding at the pro shop.
Set up the picnic by the garden fountain.
Casually steer Leo toward the garden.
Tell Harper he's on his way.

missions.title: The Flower Bed Feud
missions.description: Babs Hendricks and Diane Ross are at war over the garden beds: hydrangeas versus roses. The garden committee wants it settled.

steps.prompt: Talk to Babs about the flower beds.
How do you settle the flower beds?

choices.label: Split the bed down the middle
choices.result: Roses on the north side, hydrangeas on the south. Both women inspect the border line with a ruler. Peace, of a kind.

choices.label: Let Maria decide as co-chair
choices.result: Maria, delighted to be asked, picks hydrangeas "for the koi". Babs beams. Diane writes something in her notebook.

choices.label: Roses were there first
choices.result: Diane nods as if this were obvious. Babs says "Mm-hmm" in a way that promises the story will be all over the patio by lunch.

missions.title: Gloria's Wooden Racket
missions.description: Gloria Castellano's 1968 wooden racket snapped a string. It's on the Court 5 bench and it needs Jess, carefully.

steps.prompt: Collect Gloria's wooden racket from Court 5. Gently.
Take the racket to Jess at the pro shop.
Hand the racket over to Jess.

missions.title: Section 7.3
missions.description: Frank DeLuca has cited Kevin Park under bylaw 7.3, 'appropriate tennis attire'. Again. Kevin is hiding by the pro shop.

steps.prompt: Find Kevin and hear his side.
How do you handle the dress code dispute?

choices.label: Loan Kevin whites from the pro shop
choices.result: Kevin emerges in head-to-toe whites, looking like a 1978 tournament poster. Frank salutes. Kevin isn't sure how to feel.

choices.label: Point out 7.3 was amended in 2009
choices.result: Frank checks his binder. Then checks it again. "Amended," he says, like a man betrayed. Kevin does a very small victory dance.

choices.label: Compromise: tuck the shirt in
choices.result: Kevin tucks. Frank inspects. "Marginal," he says, and walks off. From Frank, that's practically a hug.

missions.title: Barbara the Ball Bucket
missions.description: Lily Santos has collected 47 stray balls in a hopper she named Barbara. Barbara is too heavy, and belongs in the equipment shed.

steps.prompt: Pick up Barbara (the ball hopper) at Court 4.
Give Barbara a home in the equipment shed.
Let Maria know where her daughter has been.

missions.title: Paged Mid-Serve
missions.description: Dr. Rao was paged to the hospital in the middle of his hit with Nate. His racket is still on Court 2, and Nate is still warmed up.

steps.prompt: Talk to Dr. Rao before he runs.
Collect Dr. Rao's racket from Court 2.
Leave the racket at the pro shop for safekeeping.
Nate's warmed up with nobody to hit with.

choices.label: Find Theo for him
choices.result: Theo arrives so fast he forgets to be cool. Nate grins and hands him the first serve.

choices.label: Feed him balls on your break
choices.result: You feed forty forehands. Nate thanks you politely and logs it as "sub-optimal, appreciated".

choices.label: Suggest he call it a day
choices.result: Nate looks at you like you suggested he skip a banana. He goes for a run instead.

missions.title: Lesson Setup
missions.description: Coach Rafa needs a ball hopper on Court 3 for Priya's lesson.

steps.prompt: Grab a ball hopper from the garden storage.
Set the hopper on Court 3 for the lesson.
Let Priya know her lesson is ready.

missions.title: Locker Room Linens
missions.description: The locker rooms are out of towels. Collect a fresh stack from the pool house laundry and restock the clubhouse locker rooms.

steps.prompt: Grab fresh towels from the pool house (west of the clubhouse, past the locker wing).
Restock the clubhouse locker rooms (through the lounge, down the photo corridor).

missions.title: Gym Hydration
missions.description: The fitness centre's water cooler is empty and the spin crowd is parched. Bring water bottles over from the café.

steps.prompt: Pick up a case of water from the clubhouse café bar.
Deliver the water to the Fitness & Wellness centre by the front lot.

missions.title: Fireside Seats
missions.description: A dispute over the armchairs by the lounge fireplace. Sort it out before it becomes club lore.

steps.prompt: Head to the members' lounge in the clubhouse.
Hear Gloria out about the fireside armchairs.
How do you settle the seating?

choices.label: Reserve the chairs for the champions
choices.result: You put a brass 'Club Champions' card on the armchairs. Gloria beams; the juniors grumble.

choices.label: First come, first served
choices.result: You remind everyone the lounge is for all members. Gloria sniffs, but agrees it's fair.

choices.label: Bring in a third armchair
choices.result: You drag a spare armchair over from the card table. Suddenly there's room for everyone.

missions.title: Poolside Towel Run
missions.description: Dani's towel caddy at the pool is empty and the deck is full of dripping members. Fresh towels are stacked in the locker rooms.

steps.prompt: See Dani at the lifeguard chair by the pool.
Grab a stack of fresh towels from the locker rooms in the clubhouse wing.
Bring the towels to the pool deck (side table by the lifeguard chair).
Let Dani know the towels are out.

missions.title: Lemonade for the Bridge Club
missions.description: Babs Hendricks ordered a case of Gus's lemonade for her bridge club on the patio. Gus can't leave the snack hatch.

steps.prompt: Talk to Gus at the pool house snack hatch.
Pick up the lemonade case from the snack bar counter inside the pool house.
Deliver the lemonade to the bridge table on the clubhouse patio.
Tell Babs her lemonade has arrived.

missions.title: Footwork Boot Camp
missions.description: Marcus wants to run a tennis footwork boot camp in the gym and needs a ball hopper from Court 1. Then someone has to decide who leads the warm-up.

steps.prompt: Talk to Marcus on the gym floor at the fitness centre.
Borrow the ball hopper by the Court 1 bench.
Bring the ball hopper to the gym floor in the fitness centre.
Who leads the boot camp warm-up?

choices.label: Let Frank lead it, drill-sergeant style
choices.result: Frank barks the warm-up like it's 1971. Nobody has ever split-stepped with more fear. Marcus writes 'Sergeant?' on the whiteboard and underlines it.

choices.label: Marcus runs it by the book
choices.result: Dynamic stretches, ladder drills, one hundred high-fives. Marcus is radiant. Frank does it all anyway, ten seconds faster.

choices.label: Make it a relay: Nate versus Frank
choices.result: Nate wins the cone drill by 0.4 seconds. Frank wins the push-ups by eleven. Both demand a rematch. Marcus calls it the best class of the year.

missions.title: Double-Parked
missions.description: Security's on the radio: a silver sports car is parked across two spaces and the fire lane by the gate. Otis has a guess whose it is.

steps.prompt: Meet Otis at the front gate.
Find Chad Blake and bring up his parking.
How do you sort out Chad's car?

choices.label: Ask Chad to move it now
choices.result: Chad sighs, jogs to the lot and re-parks. Crooked, but inside the lines. Otis logs it as 'resolved, aesthetically disappointing'.

choices.label: Offer to valet it yourself
choices.result: Chad tosses you the keys like it's a movie. You park it perfectly. Chad tips you a signed ball. Otis raises one eyebrow.

choices.label: Let Otis write the warning
choices.result: Otis writes the warning slowly, in pen, reading each word aloud. Chad moves the car before he finishes the second sentence.

missions.title: Lost and Found
missions.description: Otis found a racket by the perimeter fence on his patrol and left it in the locker room lost-and-found. It belongs at the pro shop, where Jess logs everything.

steps.prompt: Get the details from Otis at the front gate.
Collect the racket from the lost-and-found in the locker rooms.
Take the racket to the pro shop.
Hand the racket over to Jess for the log.

missions.title: The Greenbriar Cup
missions.description: Rafa is launching the club championship. Get the sign-up sheet posted at the pro shop.

steps.prompt: Talk to Rafa about the Cup.
Take the sign-up sheet to the pro shop.

missions.title: Cup Seeding Showdown
missions.description: Chad and Nate both claim the top seed for the Greenbriar Cup. Settle it on Court 1.

choices.label: Nate: the ladder says so
choices.result: Nate nods once. Chad announces he prefers being the underdog anyway. Loudly.

choices.label: Chad: he won last summer
choices.result: Chad does a victory lap of Court 1. Nate updates a spreadsheet, calmly, forever.

choices.label: Let them play a tiebreak for it
choices.result: Seven points later Nate is top seed, Chad wants best of three, and the crowd loves it.

missions.title: Cup Final Day
missions.description: The Greenbriar Cup final is on Court 1. Balls, water, and Mrs. Wellington presents the trophy.

steps.prompt: Get the final-day plan from Rafa.
Grab fresh balls at the equipment shed.
Pick up water at the pro shop.
Water for the finalists on Court 1.
Escort Mrs. Wellington to present the trophy.

missions.title: Hank's Old Roller
missions.description: Hank has something on his mind, and something in the shed he wants you to see.

steps.prompt: Meet Hank at the equipment shed.

choices.label: The club needs you
choices.result: Hank grunts. "Club needed rain in 1987 too. Got by." But he stands a little straighter.

choices.label: Teach me everything first
choices.result: A long look. "Tuesday. Six sharp. Bring gloves." That is a yes.

choices.label: You've earned a rest
choices.result: "Earned. Hm." He pats the roller like an old horse. "Maybe."

missions.title: Hank's Apprentice
missions.description: Hank wants to watch you groom the clay, start to finish. No pressure. Lots of pressure.

steps.prompt: Report to Hank for your lesson.
Hitch the drag brush at the equipment shed.
Groom the clay courts while Hank watches.

missions.title: Forty Years of Hank
missions.description: Gus is throwing Hank a surprise party for forty years at Greenbriar. Hank must not find out.

steps.prompt: Pick up Gus's lemonade at the pool house.
Set up the party table on the patio.
Bring Hank to the patio, casually.

missions.title: Kevin Needs a Partner
missions.description: Kevin wants to enter the doubles ladder but is too nervous to ask anyone.

steps.prompt: Ask Priya if she would partner Kevin.
How do you set it up?

choices.label: Introduce them properly
choices.result: Kevin and Priya discover they both read the rulebook for fun. A team is born.

choices.label: Book them a practice court
choices.result: Court 2, Thursday at five. Kevin has already set three reminders.

choices.label: Suggest a lesson with Rafa first
choices.result: Sensible. Slightly deflating. They both agree anyway.

missions.title: Section 7.3
missions.description: Frank has written Kevin up again. Time to broker a peace at the pro shop.

choices.label: Frank mentors Kevin on the rules
choices.result: Frank lights up. Kevin gets a laminated copy of the bylaws. Both are strangely happy.

choices.label: The rule is out of date
choices.result: Frank goes pale. Kevin is vindicated. The bylaws committee will hear of this.

choices.label: Get them on court together
choices.result: One set of doubles later, Frank calls Kevin "son". It is a compliment.

missions.title: The Board's Offer
missions.description: The club board has asked to see the Head of Grounds in the members' lounge.

steps.prompt: Diane has news from the board.
Meet Mrs. Wellington in the lounge.

choices.label: Accept: Director of Grounds
choices.result: A handshake, a brass nameplate and, somewhere, Hank laughing. The courts are yours.

choices.label: Stay on the courts, where the work is
choices.result: "Stubborn," says Mrs. Wellington. "Good." Frank salutes. Diane pretends not to be touched.

choices.label: Negotiate: a new cart first
choices.result: Diane quotes the budget from memory. You get the cart. And the title.

theo_practice_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_1.text: Hey. Okay, so. I'm supposed to be at etiquette lunch right now.

theo_practice_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_1.text: But the junior championship is in three weeks and my second serve is a disaster. I need a ball hopper on Court 1.

theo_practice_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_1.text: Quietly. If Grandma sees a hopper with my name near it, I'm doing napkin folding until I'm thirty.

theo_practice_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_2.text: You got it? No way. Thanks. Seriously.

theo_practice_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_practice_2.text: Nate says you need five hundred second serves a week. I'm at forty. ...Don't tell anyone I said thanks.

theo_grandma_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_grandma_1.text: So... I signed up for the junior championship. With my allowance. Grandma doesn't know.

theo_grandma_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_grandma_1.text: She's on the patio. She likes you. Well, she hasn't complained about you in, like, two days.

theo_grandma_1.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_grandma_1.text: Could you... bring it up? Casually? I'll be behind the fountain. Not hiding. Just... near the fountain.

theo_grandma_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_grandma_2.text: The attendant. You have the expression of someone about to say something I won't like.

theo_grandma_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_grandma_2.text: Theodore? Tennis? He has etiquette lunch. He has sailing. He has Latin.

theo_grandma_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_grandma_2.text: ...His grandfather used to sneak off to play, too. Well? Out with it.

theo_exhibition_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
theo_exhibition_1.text: Ah, my friend. You have heard? Theo plays an exhibition set on Court 1. His grandmother will watch.

theo_exhibition_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
theo_exhibition_1.text: Whatever you told her, it worked. She asked me what 'topspin' is. I told her it is a way of life.

theo_exhibition_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
theo_exhibition_1.text: Bring fresh towels from the shop. If Mrs. Wellington sits on a damp bench, Theo's career is over before it begins.

theo_exhibition_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_exhibition_2.text: She's actually here. In the front row. With a cushion she brought from home.

theo_exhibition_2.speaker: Theo Wellington
theo_exhibition_2.text: Okay. Okay. Five hundred second serves. The ball has no memory. I can do this.

theo_exhibition_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_exhibition_3.text: Six games to two. He served eleven aces. I counted. Rafa told me what an ace is.

theo_exhibition_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_exhibition_3.text: I have informed the etiquette instructor that Theodore will be unavailable on tournament weekends.

theo_exhibition_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
theo_exhibition_3.text: You were... helpful today, attendant. Do not let it go to your head.

brandt_call_1.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_call_1.text: Oh good, a neutral party. Harper lobbed me on set point. It landed behind the baseline. OUT.

brandt_call_1.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_call_1.text: I had a perfect sightline. Pilots have excellent depth perception. It's literally tested.

brandt_call_2.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_call_2.text: Okay but he was running BACKWARDS. His depth perception was aimed at the fence.

brandt_call_2.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_call_2.text: It clipped the line. There's a mark. I'd like the mark entered into evidence.

brandt_call_2.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_call_2.text: Whatever you decide, he's going to bring it up at Thanksgiving. So, you know. No pressure.

brandt_anniv_1.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_1.text: Psst! Okay, so today's our six-month anniversary, and Leo thinks I forgot. I did not forget.

brandt_anniv_1.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_1.text: I'm doing a surprise picnic by the fountain. Jess is hiding sparkling water behind the stringing machine for me.

brandt_anniv_1.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_1.text: Can you set it up in the garden, then steer Leo over? He'll be the one in lime, arguing with something.

brandt_anniv_2.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_anniv_2.text: Hey. Have you seen Harper? She's been weird all day. Weird-happy. Should I be worried?

brandt_anniv_2.speaker: Leo Brandt
brandt_anniv_2.text: The garden? Why would I... oh. OH. Is today... It's today. I'm going. I'm going right now.

brandt_anniv_3.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_3.text: He's coming? Did he remember? He didn't remember. It's okay, that's the whole point of surprises!

brandt_anniv_3.speaker: Harper Brandt
brandt_anniv_3.text: Thank you! You're getting the first slice of cake. Unless Leo eats it. He stress-eats when he's grateful.

flower_feud_1.speaker: Babs Hendricks
flower_feud_1.text: Oh, honey, thank goodness. You won't BELIEVE what Diane did to my hydrangeas.

flower_feud_1.speaker: Babs Hendricks
flower_feud_1.text: She pulled up two of them and planted roses. ROSES. Lily saw the whole thing. She's a very reliable witness. She's ten.

flower_feud_1.speaker: Babs Hendricks
flower_feud_1.text: Hydrangeas are the club flower. Well, they're MY flower. Same thing.

flower_feud_2.speaker: Diane Ross
flower_feud_2.text: That bed has had roses since 1987. I planted them. As president. Of the club. For six terms.

flower_feud_2.speaker: Diane Ross
flower_feud_2.text: Babs slipped her hydrangeas in while I was at the dentist. That's not gardening. That's a coup.

gloria_racket_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
gloria_racket_1.text: Darling. My racket has broken a string. The racket is from 1968. So am I, spiritually.

gloria_racket_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
gloria_racket_1.text: It's on the Court 5 bench. Carry it like a newborn. Jess is the only person I trust to restring it.

gloria_racket_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
gloria_racket_1.text: And if Frank asks, I'm not forfeiting. I'm merely... pausing my dominance.

gloria_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
gloria_racket_2.text: Oh. The Maxply. Hi, old friend.

gloria_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
gloria_racket_2.text: Gut strings, 50 pounds, hand-knotted. Tell Gloria tomorrow morning. Tell her I said 'with respect'. She'll know.

dress_code_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
dress_code_1.text: Attendant. Report. The Park boy is in violation of section 7.3, appropriate tennis attire.

dress_code_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
dress_code_1.text: Cargo shorts, son. With eight pockets. I counted. Nobody needs eight pockets on a tennis court.

dress_code_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
dress_code_1.text: I'm not unreasonable. I'm by the book. Take care of it.

dress_code_2.speaker: Kevin Park
dress_code_2.text: Is he gone? Oh no, he sent you. Okay. Okay.

dress_code_2.speaker: Kevin Park
dress_code_2.text: They're technical shorts! The pockets are for my phone, my backup phone, and my serve notebook.

dress_code_2.speaker: Kevin Park
dress_code_2.text: Priya says the dress code was changed years ago, but I can't find it anywhere. Nobody tells us anything...

lily_balls_1.speaker: Lily Santos
lily_balls_1.text: HI! This is Barbara! She's a ball bucket! She has FORTY-SEVEN balls in her!

lily_balls_1.speaker: Lily Santos
lily_balls_1.text: I found them in the hedges and under benches and one was in the fountain, but Gerald didn't want it.

lily_balls_1.speaker: Lily Santos
lily_balls_1.text: Barbara's at Court 4 and she's too heavy now. Can you take her to the shed? She needs a home. A good home.

lily_balls_2.speaker: Maria Santos
lily_balls_2.text: Forty-seven balls? From the hedges? That explains the scratches on her arms. And the leaves in her hair.

lily_balls_2.speaker: Maria Santos
lily_balls_2.text: Thank you for humoring her. She's going to tell everyone Barbara lives in the shed now. Hank will love that.

vik_paged_1.speaker: Dr. Vik Rao
vik_paged_1.text: I am so sorry, I have to go. Compound fracture. Mid-serve, again. The pager has impeccable timing.

vik_paged_1.speaker: Dr. Vik Rao
vik_paged_1.text: My racket's on Court 2. Could you get it to the pro shop? Jess keeps it safe from Chad.

vik_paged_1.speaker: Dr. Vik Rao
vik_paged_1.text: And tell Nate I'm sorry. He was warmed up. He hates wasting a warm-up. Medically, he's right.

vik_paged_2.speaker: Nate Okafor
vik_paged_2.text: Paged again? That's fifteen this season.

vik_paged_2.speaker: Nate Okafor
vik_paged_2.text: I'm fully warmed up. Heart rate's in the zone. It'd be a shame to waste it.

lesson_setup_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
lesson_setup_1.text: Oh, the hopper's out already? Thank you! Rafa says today is 'the day of the backhand'.

lesson_setup_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
lesson_setup_1.text: Last week was 'the day of the split step'. I split-stepped into the net. He said it was 'progress, in a way'.

opening_briefing.speaker: Hank Morris
opening_briefing.text: Morning! Clay took a beating yesterday, so keep an eye on Courts 3 to 5.

opening_briefing.speaker: Hank Morris
opening_briefing.text: Rush hours are mid-morning and late afternoon. The radio gets busy then, so pace yourself.

reservation_dispute_1.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
reservation_dispute_1.text: I have had this court reserved for WEEKS. And now this person just walks on?

reservation_dispute_1.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
reservation_dispute_1.text: Check the schedule. You'll see I'm right.

reservation_dispute_2.speaker: Kevin Park
reservation_dispute_2.text: Oh no, am I on the wrong court? The app said Court 3...

reservation_dispute_2.speaker: Kevin Park
reservation_dispute_2.text: I'm so sorry, I'm still figuring out how this place works.

patio_argument_1.speaker: Chad Blake
patio_argument_1.text: Bro, I was literally sitting here first. I went to grab a drink for TWO seconds.

patio_argument_1.speaker: Chad Blake
patio_argument_1.text: Tell her this is my table.

patio_argument_2.speaker: Diane Ross
patio_argument_2.text: This young man abandoned his table. I sat down. That's how it works.

patio_argument_2.speaker: Diane Ross
patio_argument_2.text: I've been a member here since before he was born.

wrong_court_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
wrong_court_1.text: Hey! So I signed up for Court 1 but... I think I'm on Court 3?

wrong_court_1.speaker: Priya Sharma
wrong_court_1.text: All these courts look the same to me! Is this the clay one? What's clay?

noise_complaint_1.speaker: Diane Ross
noise_complaint_1.text: Do you HEAR that racket? No pun intended.

noise_complaint_1.speaker: Diane Ross
noise_complaint_1.text: That person on Court 2 is grunting like a wild animal. Handle it.

noise_complaint_2.speaker: Tommy Chen
noise_complaint_2.text: Oh man, was I being loud? I get into the zone sometimes!

noise_complaint_2.speaker: Tommy Chen
noise_complaint_2.text: My bad, my bad. What do you think I should do?

groom_intro_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_intro_1.text: Good, you're here. All three clay courts have been getting hammered — slides, divots, the works.

groom_intro_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_intro_1.text: Head to the equipment shed and hook up the drag brush. Then start at the fence perimeter and work your way in.

groom_intro_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_intro_1.text: After the perimeter, sweep close to the nets on each court. Then fill in the middles. Don't forget to swap the coolers and check the trash bins between courts!

groom_complete_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_complete_1.text: Let me take a look... nice work out there. All three courts look great.

groom_complete_1.speaker: Hank Morris
groom_complete_1.text: Keep it up and you'll be running the grounds crew in no time.

morning_prep_1.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_1.text: Big morning ahead — all three clay courts need grooming before the 9 AM group.

morning_prep_1.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_1.text: Grab the brush, start at the fence line, and sweep your way in toward the nets. Remember to check the coolers and trash between courts.

morning_prep_1.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_1.text: I'll be checking your work when you're done, so make it count!

morning_prep_done.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_done.text: All three courts done? Let me see...

morning_prep_done.speaker: Hank Morris
morning_prep_done.text: Looking sharp! The members are going to love playing on that surface today. Good job.

bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.text: Thirty years I have sat in that chair by the fire. Thirty years!

bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.text: And today some teenager is doing his homework in it with a smoothie. On the leather.

bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.speaker: Gloria Castellano
bldg_lounge_fireplace_1.text: I'm not asking for a plaque, dear. Although a plaque would be lovely.

staff_pool_towels_1.speaker: Dani Kowalski
staff_pool_towels_1.text: Hi! Towel emergency. Not a real emergency. A towel one.

staff_pool_towels_1.speaker: Dani Kowalski
staff_pool_towels_1.text: The caddy's empty and I've got six drippy members and one very drippy Babs. I can't leave the chair.

staff_pool_towels_1.speaker: Dani Kowalski
staff_pool_towels_1.text: Fresh stacks live in the locker rooms, clubhouse wing. Bring them to the side table by my chair. Walking feet!

staff_pool_towels_2.speaker: Dani Kowalski
staff_pool_towels_2.text: Towels! You're a hero. A dry hero.

staff_pool_towels_2.speaker: Dani Kowalski
staff_pool_towels_2.text: Babs says thank you. Well, she said 'finally', but in a thank-you voice.

staff_snack_lemonade_1.speaker: Gus Papadakis
staff_snack_lemonade_1.text: Boss! Perfect timing. I got an order and no legs to deliver it.

staff_snack_lemonade_1.speaker: Gus Papadakis
staff_snack_lemonade_1.text: Babs Hendricks, bridge club, patio table. One case of Gus's famous lemonade. Extra lemon. Extra famous.

staff_snack_lemonade_1.speaker: Gus Papadakis
staff_snack_lemonade_1.text: Case is on the counter inside, snack bar side. Come round through the pool house door. Go, go, before the ice gives up.

staff_snack_lemonade_2.speaker: Babs Hendricks
staff_snack_lemonade_2.text: Oh, the lemonade! Gus is an angel. A mustached angel.

staff_snack_lemonade_2.speaker: Babs Hendricks
staff_snack_lemonade_2.text: Did he tell you anything? About anyone? No? Well. I'll pry it out of him at lunch.

staff_gym_bootcamp_1.speaker: Marcus Bell
staff_gym_bootcamp_1.text: Champ! Big idea. Footwork boot camp. Cones, ladders, split-steps, the works.

staff_gym_bootcamp_1.speaker: Marcus Bell
staff_gym_bootcamp_1.text: Problem: I have zero tennis balls and one hundred percent enthusiasm.

staff_gym_bootcamp_1.speaker: Marcus Bell
staff_gym_bootcamp_1.text: There's a ball hopper by the Court 1 bench. Borrow it, bring it to the gym floor. That's your warm-up set!

staff_gym_bootcamp_2.speaker: Marcus Bell
staff_gym_bootcamp_2.text: Hopper! Let's go! Okay, second problem.

staff_gym_bootcamp_2.speaker: Marcus Bell
staff_gym_bootcamp_2.text: Frank wants to lead the warm-up. Frank does push-ups on his knuckles. On gravel. For fun.

staff_gym_bootcamp_2.speaker: Marcus Bell
staff_gym_bootcamp_2.text: Nate says he'll only come if there's a timed drill. So. Coach's call, champ. Who runs it?

staff_security_parking_1.speaker: Otis Grant
staff_security_parking_1.text: Got a minute? We have a situation. Silver sports car. Across two spaces and the fire lane.

staff_security_parking_1.speaker: Otis Grant
staff_security_parking_1.text: Vanity plate says 'ACE CHAD'. I'm not a detective anymore. But I was.

staff_security_parking_1.speaker: Otis Grant
staff_security_parking_1.text: Find Mr. Blake and have a word. Politely. If he waves at me again, I'm writing it up.

staff_security_parking_2.speaker: Chad Blake
staff_security_parking_2.text: My car? Bro, that car is a work of art. It needs two spaces. It needs room to breathe.

staff_security_parking_2.speaker: Chad Blake
staff_security_parking_2.text: The fire lane was empty! There was no fire! What do you want me to do, drive it again?

staff_security_lost_racket_1.speaker: Otis Grant
staff_security_lost_racket_1.text: Hello. Found a racket by the perimeter fence on my six a.m. round. Black frame. Good strings.

staff_security_lost_racket_1.speaker: Otis Grant
staff_security_lost_racket_1.text: I left it in the locker room lost-and-found. It should go to the pro shop. Jess logs everything. Faster than I did at the precinct.

staff_security_lost_racket_1.speaker: Otis Grant
staff_security_lost_racket_1.text: Take it over when you get a minute. Chain of custody. Old habit.

staff_security_lost_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
staff_security_lost_racket_2.text: A racket. From the fence. Of course.

staff_security_lost_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
staff_security_lost_racket_2.text: Fifty-two pounds, cross strings a little loose. That's Rafa's backup. He's been looking for it since Tuesday.

staff_security_lost_racket_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
staff_security_lost_racket_2.text: Tell Otis thanks. I'm adding him to the chart. The good chart.

cup_signup_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
cup_signup_1.text: Ah, just the person. The board has approved the Greenbriar Cup. Singles, all levels, one trophy.

cup_signup_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
cup_signup_1.text: A tournament is like bread. It needs a starter. Take this sign-up sheet to Jess at the pro shop.

cup_signup_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
cup_signup_1.text: And watch Chad. He will try to sign up twice.

cup_signup_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
cup_signup_2.text: The Cup sheet. Great. I will pin it by the register.

cup_signup_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
cup_signup_2.text: Chad already emailed asking if he can be seeded first "by vibes". I replied with a blank email.

cup_signup_2.speaker: Jess Nakamura
cup_signup_2.text: Thanks. That is one less thing between me and my lunch.

cup_seeding_1.speaker: Chad Blake
cup_seeding_1.text: Okay. Okay. Top seed. ME. I won the summer social. I have a signature fist pump. Seeds are about ENERGY.

cup_seeding_1.speaker: Chad Blake
cup_seeding_1.text: Nate is great. Nate is a spreadsheet with legs. You cannot seed a spreadsheet.

cup_seeding_2.speaker: Nate Okafor
cup_seeding_2.text: Ladder rating: me, 1480. Chad, 1391. Head to head: four and two.

cup_seeding_2.speaker: Nate Okafor
cup_seeding_2.text: I respect the fist pump. I respect math more. Your call.

cup_final_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
cup_final_1.text: Final day. The court must be ready like a table before guests. Balls, water, nothing on the lines.

cup_final_1.speaker: Coach Rafa Ibarra
cup_final_1.text: When it is done, bring Mrs. Wellington. She presents the trophy. Her grandfather bought it.

cup_final_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
cup_final_2.text: The Greenbriar Cup. My grandfather commissioned it in 1961. It has never looked so clean.

cup_final_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
cup_final_2.text: The court is immaculate. The water is cold. I have no complaints, which I find unsettling.

cup_final_2.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
cup_final_2.text: Thank you, attendant. No. Thank you, by name. I shall learn it.

hank_roller_1.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_roller_1.text: Got a minute? Walk with me to the shed. Something I want you to see.

hank_roller_1.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_roller_1.text: Do not look at me like that. It is not a body. It is a roller.

hank_roller_2.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_roller_2.text: First roller this club ever bought. 1983. I rolled every court with her until my knees filed a union grievance.

hank_roller_2.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_roller_2.text: Board asked if I am thinking of retiring. I said I would think about it. Now I cannot stop thinking about it.

hank_roller_2.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_roller_2.text: You are good on the clay. Better than I was at your age. So. What do you reckon?

hank_apprentice_1.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_apprentice_1.text: Lesson day. I watch, you drag. Perimeter first, then the nets, then the middles.

hank_apprentice_1.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_apprentice_1.text: If you miss a corner I will say nothing. Silence is worse. Off you go.

hank_apprentice_2.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_apprentice_2.text: That is the best "hm" I have given in twenty years. Do not tell anyone.

hank_apprentice_2.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_apprentice_2.text: Crops come up straight when the soil is right. You are right. Good.

hank_party_1.speaker: Gus Papadakis
hank_party_1.text: Boss. Come here. Closer. Hank has been at this club forty years this week.

hank_party_1.speaker: Gus Papadakis
hank_party_1.text: We are doing a party. Surprise. Lemonade is in the pool house. Patio table, discreet.

hank_party_1.speaker: Gus Papadakis
hank_party_1.text: If he asks, you are "checking umbrellas". He hates umbrellas. He will not follow you.

hank_party_2.speaker: Babs Hendricks
hank_party_2.text: Honey, the banner says "FORTY YEARS OF HANK" in gold, and I did not ask anyone first, and I regret nothing.

hank_party_2.speaker: Babs Hendricks
hank_party_2.text: Bob made a toast. It is eleven minutes long. I cut it to nine. Go get the man!

hank_party_3.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_party_3.text: Patio? Why would I go to the... what is all this.

hank_party_3.speaker: Hank Morris
hank_party_3.text: Forty years. Huh. Somebody pass me a lemonade before I say something soft.

kevin_doubles_1.speaker: Kevin Park
kevin_doubles_1.text: Hi! Um. So the doubles ladder opens this week, and I would really like to join, and you need a partner, and...

kevin_doubles_1.speaker: Kevin Park
kevin_doubles_1.text: ...I have made a list of possible partners. It is one person. Priya. Could you... ask her? For me? Sorry.

kevin_doubles_2.speaker: Priya Sharma
kevin_doubles_2.text: Kevin wants to play doubles with me? Oh! Sorry, one more thing: is he good? Does it matter? I am not good either.

kevin_doubles_2.speaker: Priya Sharma
kevin_doubles_2.text: Yes. Tell him yes. Wait. How do you think we should start?

kevin_frank_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
kevin_frank_1.text: Son, Kevin Park has violated section 7.3 for the fourth time. Untucked shirt. On a Tuesday.

kevin_frank_1.speaker: Frank DeLuca
kevin_frank_1.text: I have written a memo. I have written a memo about the memo. Standards, son.

kevin_frank_2.speaker: Kevin Park
kevin_frank_2.text: I tucked it! It came untucked during a serve. I think that is just physics? Sorry.

kevin_frank_2.speaker: Kevin Park
kevin_frank_2.text: He is kind of scary but he also taught me how to hold a volley once, so I do not know how to feel.

board_offer_1.speaker: Diane Ross
board_offer_1.text: Excuse me. A moment. The board met on Tuesday. Item seven was you.

board_offer_1.speaker: Diane Ross
board_offer_1.text: Courts at ninety percent or better for a month. Member complaints down. Babs is happy, which is statistically improbable.

board_offer_2.speaker: Frank DeLuca
board_offer_2.text: Son. At ease. The board would like to offer you a position. With a title. And a desk.

board_offer_2.speaker: Frank DeLuca
board_offer_2.text: I voted for you. Twice. The second vote did not count, but I wanted it on the record.

board_offer_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
board_offer_3.text: Sit. The board wishes to name you Director of Grounds. My grandfather created the post. It has been empty since 1994.

board_offer_3.speaker: Mrs. Wellington
board_offer_3.text: Hank recommended you. Hank has never recommended anyone. So. Your answer?
